abstract_sentences.text: Non-monotonic sequence generation methods, such as masked diffusion models, provide a flexible alternative to left-to-right autoregressive modeling by allowing tokens to be generated in non-fixed and prescribed orders.

Despite their practical advantages, most existing non-monotonic models are order-agnostic and rely on a fixed-length grid, limiting their ability to support variable-length generation and adaptive insertion order.

evidence.anchor: order-agnostic and rely on a fixed-length grid

abstract_sentences.text: In this work, we introduce a probabilistic framework for learning insertion order in variable-length insertion models.

evidence.anchor: probabilistic framework for learning insertion order

abstract_sentences.text: We formalize a bijective correspondence between insertion trajectories and permutations, which enables an exact reparameterization of the data likelihood as a sum over permutations.

evidence.anchor: bijective correspondence between insertion trajectories and permutations

abstract_sentences.text: Building on this result, we propose the Insertion Process (IP), a stochastic generative model that jointly learns where to insert, what to insert, and when to terminate, trained via permutation-based variational inference.
Unlike prior fixed-canvas approaches, IP natively supports variable-length generation and learns data-driven preferences over insertion orders.

Experiments on goal-conditioned planning and molecular string generation demonstrate that learning insertion order improves both modeling quality and generalization in domains without a canonical left-to-right structure.

experimental_design.name: Research questions
experimental_design.description: Three stated questions concern insertion versus AR, learned versus order-agnostic policy, and transfer to planning/flexible-length conditional generation.

evidence.anchor: Our experiments are designed to answer

experimental_design.name: Maze planning data
experimental_design.description: Synthetic grid-maze paths with ordered subgoals; Appendix D.1 gives 80/10/10 splits and default m=20, max path length 400.

experimental_design.name: Star-graph planning data
experimental_design.description: Hard directed star graphs use degree 5, arm lengths 6–12, vocabulary size 56, and predict the directed path after a randomly ordered edge-list prefix.

experimental_design.name: Molecular data and tasks
experimental_design.description: GuacaMol supports unconditional SMILES generation and four slot-constrained conditional fragment/linker tasks; Table 4 uses 1024 samples per task.

experimental_design.name: Baselines and control matching
experimental_design.description: FO-ARM, AO-ARM, MDM and LO-ARM are stated baselines; AO-IP fixes a random insertion policy; planning says baselines share the architecture.

evidence.anchor: all baselines use the same architecture

experimental_design.name: Planning training
experimental_design.description: 100 epochs, batch 64, AdamW, 1e-4 learning rate, cosine decay, 1000 warmup steps, EMA 0.999, a 12-layer decoder and RLOO M=2 are reported.

evidence.anchor: We train on two planning datasets for 100 epochs

experimental_design.name: GuacaMol training
experimental_design.description: The generative decoder has 18 attention layers and the VI encoder 3 layers; Table 5 supplies optimizer and learning-rate entries.

experimental_design.name: Random seeds, run count, hardware, and wall-clock
experimental_design.description: The read PDF supplies no seed list, repetition count, hardware specification, or wall-clock budget.

experimental_design.name: Leakage controls and failure threshold
experimental_design.description: Splits and task conditioning are described, but no independent leakage audit or predeclared failure threshold is stated.

result_inventory.claim: IP is strongest across reported maze cells.

result_inventory.claim: IP has much higher reported conditional validity than AO-IP.

result_inventory.claim: The learned insertion trace commonly stages structural markers before atom insertion.

result_inventory.comparison: No human grammar or alternative-mechanism comparator is quantified.

ablation_inventory.name: Any-Order IP (AO-IP)
ablation_inventory.description: The stated random-insertion-policy variant tests whether learning the insertion order matters. Its unconditional validity is 88.2 versus 97.4 for classifier-based IP and its conditional validity is lower in all four listed tasks.

claim_closure.claim: Variable-length insertion can learn data-dependent order.
claim_closure.method_response: IP jointly predicts slot, token, and termination, with a PL posterior over permutations.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Planning and molecular results include AO-IP comparisons.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates the insertion generative model and two domains.

evidence.anchor: where to insert, what to insert, and when to terminate

claim_closure.claim: Trajectory-dependent actions admit a fixed latent representation for likelihood training.
claim_closure.method_response: The method uses global σ and z_i=f(σ≤i).
claim_closure.evidence_response: Lemma 2.1 and Theorem 2.2 are proven in Appendix A rather than empirically tested.

claim_closure.claim: Learning order improves quality and generalization in domains without canonical left-to-right structure.
claim_closure.method_response: The model is built for variable-length insertion and instance-specific order.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Two planning families and SMILES show reported comparisons, but no seeds or outside-domain test are reported.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion calls the method effective in two domains and suggests protein design future work.

claim_closure.claim: The learned schedule internalizes SMILES structural rules.
claim_closure.method_response: The PL posterior can express instance-specific token orders.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 5, the 99.7% pattern and AO-IP comparison are consistent with the interpretation; no independent mechanism intervention occurs.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion does not return to this mechanism claim separately.

final_judgment.single_storyline: A trajectory-to-permutation bijection supplies a fixed latent order for variational training of a variable-length insertion generator, then planning and SMILES comparisons test the learned order.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The core process, two named results, the estimator algorithm, baseline rationale, four main result tables, and one generation trace remain in the main body.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, full policy/classifier objective derivations, dataset construction, metric definitions, hyperparameters, and qualitative galleries move to Appendix A–F.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2, then Lemma/Theorem 2.1–2.2, then the near-neighbor AO-IP comparison make the model, formalization, and targeted empirical contrast mutually legible.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Seeds, repetition counts, test denominators, dispersion, hardware, wall-clock, and an independent mechanism intervention are unavailable in the read PDF.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: When local generation actions have history-dependent coordinates, seek a fixed global latent object with a provable trajectory mapping and connect that mapping to a close empirical contrast.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule requires an identifiable one-to-one mapping and tractable enumeration or sampling of the global object; the paper does not establish it for arbitrary structured generation.

evidence.anchor: improves both modeling quality and generalization

method_logic.formal_objects: Observed target y_L; partial sequence y_i; insertion slot z_i; token x_i; global permutation σ; decoder p_φ; PL posterior q_θ.
method_logic.input_output_state: Generation starts at empty y_0, samples a slot or TERM and a token, updates y_i, and outputs the prior state when TERM occurs.
method_logic.objective: Policy termination plus permutation ELBO; classifier termination is an augmented EOS ELBO.
method_logic.assumptions: For Lemma 2.1, y_L is fixed and the insertion trajectory is valid; the state update is deterministic.
component_problem_map: global permutation resolves trajectory-dependent slot coordinates
PL plus Gumbel–Top-k samples discrete order posterior
exact conditional inner expectation and RLOO address variance/non-differentiability
explicit TERM or EOS supports variable length
method_logic.algorithm: One while-training loop and one loop over M sampled permutations; no asymptotic complexity statement is present.
